sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fiduciary Administration of Irrevocable Offshore Spendthrift Trusts

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified statutes of the Napoleonic continental tradition; Article 2 of the Constitution of 2014 declares the principles of Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation, governing personal-status matters and the structuring of Sharia-compliant financial products)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty between the United States of America and the Arab Republic of Egypt Concerning the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (entered into force 27 June 1992)

Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital in the Arab States (League of Arab States, in force since 1981; Egypt is a Contracting State and the agreement applies to intra-Arab investment flows)
Euro-Mediterranean Agreement establishing an Association between the European Communities and Egypt (in force 2004), including investment, establishment and capital-movement provisions

Bilateral investment protection and double-taxation instruments in force between Egypt and the country of the settlor and ultimate beneficial owner, to be confirmed against the GAFI and Ministry of Foreign Affairs treaty list at the time of filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and subsequent amendments; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 953 of 2003, as amended; Law No. 72 of 2017 on Investment and Executive Regulations Decree No. 2310 of 2017 regarding beneficial-ownership identification and incorporation; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended; Capital Market Law No. 95 of 1992 and Financial Regulatory Authority decrees for non-bank financial intermediation and fiduciary services; Central Bank of Egypt and Banking Law No. 194 of 2020; Egyptian Money Laundering Combating Unit administrative instructions; national terrorist-listing procedures under Law No. 8 of 2015

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the discretionary trust deed and all amendments
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the trust formation jurisdiction and the corporate records of the trustee
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (through the competent authority in the state of origin; documents originating from non-Contracting States must follow chain consular legalization at the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the proposed corporate trustee or controlling corporate board entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry / registrar of companies in the trustee jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, with translation of the certificate into Arabic by a licensed sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of the settlor, protector and identified discretionary beneficiaries, with notary certification of likeness
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the passport-issuing country or in the country of permanent residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization through the Egyptian diplomatic post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the trust account title and for the ultimate beneficial owner, issued within the 90-day pre-filing period
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank of the settlor and the trust in the principal banking relationship jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature authentication by the issuing bank and, where demanded by Egyptian counterparties, consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form and organizational chart memorandum executed for the Egyptian register, signed in person by each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant and foreign corporate services provider, with notarized signatures taken before the Egyptian Notary Public or an Egyptian Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization or apostille where the execution state is a Contracting State to the 1961 Apostille Convention

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; relevant provisions: Articles 8, 24-25 and 40 of the Companies Law, together with Executive Regulations and Law No. 34 of 2020 on Commercial Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Department, in coordination with the Commercial Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: GAFI Standard Incorporation Dossier (Application Form No. 1, Arabic Articles of Association, and Share Subscription Schedule)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under Companies Law No. 159/1981, an LLC must have a minimum nominal capital of EGP 50,000, fully subscribed at formation; at least 50% of the capital must be paid up before registration and deposited in an Egyptian bank account opened for the company under formation. The bank's Capital Deposit Certificate must be submitted to GAFI, and the deposited funds remain restricted until issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. The unpaid balance must be settled within five years. No separate statutory escrow account is required for LLC formation; the restricted bank deposit serves as the applicable capital control mechanism.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the subscribers' acceptance of the share subscriptions in [Company] is confirmed, with each subscriber taking the number of shares set opposite his name in the Subscription Schedule, and that the initial capital shall remain deposited in the company's formation account subject to the Capital Deposit Certificate until the certificate of incorporation is issued. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the registered office of the Company shall be established at [Address], Egypt. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the directors and managers named in the formation file are appointed, and the General Manager is authorised to open trust accounts, engage administrative staff, and complete all registrations with GAFI, the FRA and the competent authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (online portal or Investor Services Center)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation application through GAFI's online portal. Verify that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company or registered mark, and ensure the legal form is stated as 'Limited Liability Company'. Pay the reservation fee and obtain the Name Availability Certificate. Then have all shareholders or their lawful attorneys sign the Arabic Articles of Association and the share subscription schedule, and authenticate the signatures before an Egyptian Notary Public.
required_dossiers: Name availability application
Proposed corporate name and shareholder list
Passport copies of all shareholders and managers
Notarized power of attorney if signing through an attorney
Draft Articles of Association and Subscription Schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or inconsistency, the incorporators may immediately reserve a secondary name or file a written objection with GAFI; corrected name submissions are processed expeditedly and require no duplicate notarization if Articles are adjusted solely for name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Capital Deposit and Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed Egyptian commercial bank selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional bank account in the name of the company under formation. Deposit no less than 50% of the subscribed LLC capital into the account. Instruct the bank to issue a Capital Deposit Certificate addressed to GAFI. The deposited amounts may not be withdrawn before issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. Given the high-risk trust activity classification, the bank may apply enhanced KYC procedures and require source-of-wealth statements.
required_dossiers: Name Availability Certificate
Draft Articles of Association
Proposed registered office address
KYC/AML declarations for each subscriber
Source of funds/wealth evidence for discretionary trust administration activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional source-of-wealth documentation, provide notarized declarations and audited financial statements; if the bank declines the account due to perceived trust-related risk, select another licensed Egyptian bank and resubmit the account opening file with the same formation dossiers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department / Commercial Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed GAFI Form No. 1, notarized Arabic Articles of Association, Capital Deposit Certificate, registered office lease or title deed, and the pro-forma first board resolution. Pay the official incorporation and commercial registration fees. GAFI will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and record the company in the Commercial Registry. After incorporation, obtain the tax card number from the Egyptian Tax Authority based on the Commercial Registration Extract.
required_dossiers: GAFI Form No. 1 incorporation application
Notarized Arabic Articles of Association
Capital Deposit Certificate
Registered office lease contract or title deed
Pro-forma First Board Resolution appointing managers
Passport copies and criminal record extracts of managers
Financial statements or bank certificate reflecting paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues an inquiry or rejection, respond within the statutory period by correcting the deficient clauses and re-notarizing the Articles if necessary; if the application is refused, appeal to the GAFI Vice Chairman for Investor Affairs or re-file an amended incorporation dossier with the same reservation number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Insurance and Statistical Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI), and Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Commercial Registration Extract, complete tax registration by submitting the company formation documents to the ETA tax office. Obtain the tax card, register for VAT if the expected taxable turnover exceeds the threshold, and collect payroll/stamp duty books. Register any Egyptian resident employees with NOSI and provide the required statistical returns to CAPMAS for the ISIC 6430 fiduciary services classification.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial Registration Extract
Notarized Articles of Association
Registered office lease and utility bill
IDs and appointment resolutions of managers
Ultimate Beneficial Ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA requests further clarifications regarding the trust administration business, submit an explanatory letter and the FRA license application receipt; if a temporary delay occurs, request a provisional tax card while the tax office reviews the UBOS and AML declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Specialized Fiduciary Trust Licensing and AML Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) - Non-Bank Financial Activities Licensing Directorate, in coordination with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the special license application for the administration of discretionary asset-protection trusts. Submit the trust administration business plan, AML/CFT compliance program, internal governance manual, capital adequacy declaration, and policies covering irrevocable offshore spendthrift trusts. FRA may refer the file to the AML unit for clearance owing to the High-Risk Special License classification. The license imposes conditions on segregated client accounts, beneficial ownership monitoring, and annual compliance audits.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Commercial Registration Extract
Board Resolution approving the license application
AML/CFT Compliance Program and designated Compliance Officer
Governance manual and organizational chart
Capital adequacy and solvency statement
Business plan for irrevocable offshore spendthrift trust fiduciary services
Criminal record certificates for directors and senior managers
Settlor and beneficiary risk-assessment framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FRA issues a clarification request, respond within the prescribed period with supplementary policies or internal controls; if the application is denied, appeal to the FRA Board of Directors within thirty days, or otherwise restructure the proposed activity and resubmit with enhanced compliance safeguards.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defense Certificate and Physical Premises Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Directorate of Civil Defense under the Ministry of Interior and the Local Municipality Building Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange an inspection of the registered office, records vault, and any physical trust documentation storage. Obtain the Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate confirming fire extinguishers, emergency exits, alarm systems, and evacuation arrangements. For multi-storey premises, obtain the municipality occupancy clearance and structural load approval under the Egyptian Building Code. Since the business is office-based and not industrial, no environmental hazard license is required for the physical premises.
required_dossiers: Signed lease contract or title deed for the registered office
Floor plan and premises use classification
Fire alarm and extinguisher maintenance contracts
Civil Defense application form
Structural safety certificate from a licensed engineer
Emergency evacuation plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Civil Defense inspection identifies non-compliance, remedy the defects and request a re-inspection; if the building lacks occupancy clearance, relocate to compliant commercial premises and file the address change with GAFI and the Commercial Registry before re-applying for Civil Defense approval.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) - Non-Bank Financial Activities Licensing Directorate, in coordination with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: FRA Specialized Trust/Fiduciary Asset-Protection Services License for Discretionary Offshore Trust Administration under the FRA Non-Bank Financial Activities framework

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Compliance and Environmental Impact Assessment Department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Exempt from Full EIA Report; the activity is a licensed office and fiduciary financial service with no industrial manufacturing process, requiring only EEAA registration and a simplified environmental checklist if a records vault or backup generator is installed
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission permit is applicable to trust administration; office waste must comply with municipal solid waste regulations; electronic records destruction must comply with e-waste handling requirements; if an emergency backup generator is used, exhaust emissions, fuel storage quantities, and prevention of soil contamination must meet the thresholds and controls of Law No. 4/1994 and its Executive Regulations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate from the General Directorate of Civil Defense confirming structural fire safety and emergency egress; municipal building occupancy permit confirming structural load compliance; Ministry of Manpower workplace clearance covering safe storage of paper and electronic records, staff facilities, occupational hygiene, and emergency evacuation preparedness

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Official Portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg / https://tax.gov.eg (e-services)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign resident entity must appoint a local tax representative, file a registration application with the competent ETA office, submit authenticated constitutional documents (memorandum of association, power of attorney, passport copies), and receive a Tax Identification Number (TIN) within 15 to 30 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or deemed pass-through election under Egyptian tax law; an LLC is mandatorily taxed at the entity level. Multinational taxpayers may apply treaty/MLI relief, but no unilateral hybrid-loss election; CFC and thin-cap rules may impose recharacterization.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67/2016
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies (mandatory); voluntary registration for persons making taxable supplies above EGP 50,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The ETA has mandated electronic invoicing (e-invoice) and electronic receipts (e-receipt) through its clearance APIs. In-scope businesses must establish direct integration via the ETA e-invoice portal, generate invoices in the XML/JSON standardized format, obtain a unique ETA-accepted QR code, and transmit invoice data in real time. Non-integration or fraudulent clearance exposes the taxpayer to suspension of transactions and penalty under Ministerial Decree No. 824 of 2021.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods and services qualifies for 0% VAT where title passes to a non-resident recipient and goods leave Egypt within 90 days from the invoice date, and services are supplied to a non-resident outside Egypt, subject to documentary proof and arm's-length consideration.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or unsupported zero-rating claims trigger additional VAT, late-payment interest at approximately 14% per annum, fines from 30% to 300% of tax due, criminal penalties for deliberate fraud, and the exclusion of further refund claims. The ETA may claw back refunds and treat non-compliance with the 180-day FX repatriation requirement as a presumption of non-export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE; Al-Bank al-Markazi al-Masry), acting under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law), Foreign Exchange Decree No. 3765 of 2017, and CBE FX circulars. The Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) concurrently licenses and supervises fiduciary and trust services in Egypt; the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (ECML) supervises the AML/CFT perimeter for designated non-financial businesses and professions (DNFBPs).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations: the EGP is fully convertible on current-account flows, including service-fee remittances and profit distribution, once the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) clearance and audited financial statements are filed. Capital-account transactions (shareholder capital injection, trust corpus inflows) are convertible on a document-backed basis subject to CBE reporting and verification of the underlying under Decree No. 3765 of 2017. Following the March 2024 exchange-rate unification and the IMF-supported float, the official and parallel-market rates have converged; residual controls consist of bank-side transactional supporting-document review and FX position limits rather than quantitative ceilings. For offshore irrevocable discretionary spendthrift trust administration, distribution of fiduciary proceeds to non-resident beneficiaries is treated as a current-account service payment requiring the trust deed, distribution instructions, and beneficiary due-diligence and PEP screening; no profit-in-kind surrender is imposed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The LLC is a fiduciary-services provider, not a goods exporter; the CBE treats cross-border administration fees as service-export proceeds. Repatriation rule: all service-export receipts must be credited through an Egyptian bank within 180 days from the invoice date, with a possible CBE extension to 360 days on application. Mandatory conversion ratio: currently nil; proceeds may be retained in an onshore foreign-currency account, although the CBE encourages conversion to EGP for reserve management. A CBE statistics declaration is mandatory for any single service receipt exceeding USD 10,000, and the underlying administration contract must be archived. Late repatriation is penalised under CBE sanctions and may trigger suspension of FX market access.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Segregated Fiduciary Trust Escrow Account (USD/EGP) plus LLC Operational Account
Fiduciary Escrow Account and Operational Account (USD/EGP)
Primary USD Clearing and Fiduciary Trust Account plus EGP Operating Account
Offshore-correspondent USD sweep account mirrored to the fiduciary ledger
Operational Treasury Account (EGP) and incoming SWIFT collection account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium as a standalone settlement rail; acceptable only as a collection gateway. Egypt does not recognise offshore EMI licences; only CBE-licensed banks and payment institutions under Payments Law No. 18 of 2019 may hold Egyptian-resident funds on a fiduciary basis. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Revolut) may be used to receive remittances from the offshore trustees, but funds must be swept into the CBE-licensed bank account within two business days. Maintaining the LLC's treasury house account at an unlicensed EMI exposes the entity to ECML censure, Decree No. 3765 of 2017 violations, and bank de-risking if the onshore bank detects the pattern.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for the Egyptian resident general manager and at least two authorised signatories at the bank's designated onboarding branch; account activation requires a site inspection of the trust administration office. Remote opening is not available for high-risk DNFBP/TCSP clients. Non-resident directors and the offshore protector may execute a notarised power of attorney legalised at the Egyptian consulate, but a video-recorded AML interview with the bank's chief compliance officer is mandatory, and a senior compliance committee must ratify the file. The trust deed and any amendments must be translated into English by a licensed translator and certified before the compliance interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trust and company service providers (TCSPs) are automatic high-risk DNFBPs under Article 5 of AML Law No. 80 of 2016; onboarding triggers enhanced due diligence (EDD), a compliance committee review, and unresolved questions on the offshore trust's beneficial-ownership cascade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a valid FRA trust-services authorisation or an Egyptian Bar-qualified legal opinion proving that the Egyptian office performs only back-office administration of the offshore irrevocable discretionary trust; a board-approved AML/CFT policy; the curriculum vitae and CBE registration of an Egypt-resident compliance officer; a client-risk-rating matrix; a beneficial-ownership register extract from the Egyptian Commercial Registry; and an executed engagement letter appointing an external AML auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity — an irrevocable offshore spendthrift trust has discretionary beneficiaries and protector rights that obscure the natural-person ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified trust deed and any deeds of amendment; the protector's written declaration of reserved powers; a CBE beneficial-ownership statement identifying each beneficiary with 10% or more enjoyment rights; a source-of-wealth and source-of-funds file on the trust corpus (opening bank statements, sale-and-purchase agreements, inheritance or settlement documents); and a written jurisdiction-risk analysis of the trust's situs (e.g., Jersey, BVI, DIFC).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border 'abnormal jurisdiction' flow patterns — incoming wires from the offshore trust correspondent to the Egyptian LLC with onward distributions to foreign beneficiaries trigger transaction-monitoring alerts and address-mismatch flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Administration agreement and fee schedule; per-transaction invoices; the CBE service-export declaration for fee receipts; correspondence from the offshore trustee naming the remitter's UBO; beneficiary AML and PEP clearances against UN, OFAC, EU, UK, and CBE sanctions lists; and a signed undertaking to pre-notify the bank of every distribution batch and any change of beneficiaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP hits — discretionary beneficiaries or incoming counterparties appear on screening lists or are nationals or residents of restricted jurisdictions, resulting in Level 2 account restrictions or suspension.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative screening screenshots across UN Security Council, OFAC, EU, UK, and CBE watchlists; for any PEP hit, a detailed EDD file with source-of-funds evidence and senior-management approval; where restricted-jurisdiction persons are actual or potential beneficiaries, an external counsel legal opinion and an irrevocable undertaking to distribute no funds to sanctioned persons, with a segregate-and-return mechanism mapped out before onboarding.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All injections must flow via SWIFT MT103 to the CBE-licensed onshore foreign-currency account. Remittance purpose codes: '621 — foreign direct investment in services' or '112 — capital increase in cash' per the CBE balance-of-payments format; field 72 must state the Commercial Registration Number and the trust file reference. Supporting pack: capital-increase board resolution; GAFI-updated Commercial Register extract; ETA tax card; CBE Foreign-Currency Deposit Form countersigned by the compliance officer; and an originator-bank vetting certificate evidencing that the sender is a CBE-white-listed correspondent. The bank must suspend the wire if the originating entity is an unlicensed money-service business, an offshore EMI, or a virtual-asset exchange; therefore the originator must be the offshore trustee bank or the parent company's bank, never a crypto gateway.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements use SWIFT MT103 (bank-to-bank) for operational payments, distributions to beneficiaries, and fee remittances; trade settlements use irrevocable documentary letters of credit on MT700 subject to ICC UCP 600, or standby letters of credit (MT760) only where permitted by the trust deed. The bank file must contain the trust distribution resolution, underlying administration invoices, and, where a disbursement is a fee to a non-resident fiduciary, the CBE services-payments declaration and ETA withholding-tax certificate when the counterparty is an Egyptian taxpayer. Payments to FATF-listed or low-AML-score jurisdictions require an additional EDD memorandum and, for amounts above USD 25,000, notification to the ECML via the bank's money-laundering reporting officer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forward contracts (USD/EGP, EUR/EGP) with tenors up to 12 months, documented by genuine fiduciary-asset exposure and executed under IFEMA/ISDA terms with a CBE-licensed counterparty bank.
FX swaps (spot-against-forward) for liquidity-buffer management, tenors limited to 12 months and pre-approved by the CBE market conduct desk when volumes exceed USD 10 million equivalent per annum.

Onshore cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP) to hedge long-term trust liabilities, permitted only where the swap counterparty is a CBE-licensed bank and the transaction is reported to the CBE financial statistics department.

Offshore EGP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are expressly impermissible for Egyptian-resident entities and void under Decree No. 3765 of 2017; hedging of EGP exposure for foreign beneficiaries should instead be executed by the offshore trustee as principal in its own name.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the fiscal year end; for a 31 December fiscal year end, filing due no later than 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to EGP 500 per month or part month, delay interest on unpaid tax, enforced collection measures, and possible criminal sanction under the Unified Tax Procedures Law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registry confirmation and fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days following the commercial registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee for delayed payment, administrative suspension of the commercial register entry, and prohibition on executing registered activities while registration is non-compliant

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO information confirmation under AML/CFT requirements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 March for the preceding reporting year, and within 30 days of any change in ultimate beneficial ownership or shareholding transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under AML Law No. 80/2002, criminal liability for false disclosure, and possible revocation of the special fiduciary license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual special license renewal for fiduciary trust administration services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent financial services licensing authority (FRA and/or CBE as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 31 March; renewal application opens 60 days before the expiry of the current license year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic suspension of the license, administrative fines per day of continued operation without renewal, and cancellation of the authorization to administer trusts after 30 days of non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based exemption applies to a licensed trust administration LLC; the high-risk special fiduciary license, combined with management of third-party trust assets, makes a mandatory independent audit compulsory immediately upon licensing and each subsequent fiscal year
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are substantially aligned with IFRS; additional IFRS reporting is required for parent, consolidated, or sector-specific regulated reporting where applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under AML Law No. 80/2002 and its executive regulations, the LLC must maintain a current UBO register and annually confirm UBO data to the Egyptian FIU; any shareholding transfer or change of beneficial ownership must be recorded and reported within 30 days of the transaction, while the annual confirmation consolidates all movements as at the reporting year end

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egypt Investment Law No. 72/2017: investment deduction of 30%–80% of qualifying capital costs; tax holiday up to 10 years for projects located in free zones and the Suez Canal Economic Zone; 5-year reduction of taxable profit for new enterprises in designated frontier governorates; additional statutory deductions for research and development and employment of certain categories of labor.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Corporate Tax Return Form No. 1 (Tax on Commercial and Industrial Profits) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority e-filing portal at https://eta.gov.eg.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, subject to quarterly provisional tax payments during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final annual corporate income tax return must be filed within four months after the close of the tax year. Provisional tax instalments are generally due by the end of the third, sixth, ninth, and twelfth months of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax card number, trade register number, and full address of the Egyptian LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the filing is for a non-resident company acting through a permanent establishment (PE), insert the exact Egyptian PE registration and tax card number, and state the name of the foreign head office in parentheses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the fiscal year covered by the return; balances should agree with the audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact activation and closing date of the Egyptian permanent establishment; a short-period return is accepted when the PE commences or ceases during the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenues from trust administration, fiduciary management, management fees, and other operating income before deduction of expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Egyptian-source revenues attributable to the PE should be included; income from offshore fiduciary activities performed entirely outside Egypt may be excluded if supported by a transfer pricing analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 11 – Taxable Profit and Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of deductible expenses, allowable losses, charges, and application of the 22.5% corporate rate to arrive at net corporate tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must allocate legal, administrative, and management expenses on an arm's length basis; unallocated or disproportionate overseas head-office charges are not deductible without a valid transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosed related-party transactions cross-referenced to the transfer pricing documentation; mandatory when the aggregate threshold is exceeded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Furnish full details of any cross-border transactions between the non-resident parent, the trust, and the Egyptian PE, including contractual rates and the economic substance analysis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form No. 1 attracts a fine of EGP 5,000–20,000 for corporate taxpayers. Late payment of assessed tax attracts a monthly surcharge of 1.5% of the unpaid tax, capped at 100% of the tax due. Failure to maintain or submit required tax records can trigger additional administrative fines and criminal tax evasion penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends distributed by an Egyptian LLC to shareholders, irrespective of residence; reduced treaty rates may apply where a tax treaty election is approved.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before paying the dividend, interest, or royalty, the Egyptian withholding agent must receive a benefit owner declaration and a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign jurisdiction, with a certified Arabic translation. The claimant must obtain prior approval or a treaty relief ruling from the Egyptian Tax Authority; alternatively, where tax has been withheld at source at the domestic rate, the non-resident may file a refund claim within five years from the end of the calendar year in which the withholding occurred.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are subject to statutory withholding at 20% and are generally reduced to a 10%–12% rate under Egypt's double tax agreements. Interest paid to non-residents is subject to statutory withholding at 20% and is generally reduced to 5%–15% under applicable treaties, subject to arm's length criteria and beneficial ownership evidence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8,000,000 aggregate annual controlled transactions with related parties triggers mandatory preparation and submission of a Local File; a Master File is separately required for multinational groups with consolidated turnover above EGP 200,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt applies economic substance and anti-avoidance doctrines under Law No. 91 of 2005, including the arm's length standard for related-party transactions, controlled foreign company rules, and beneficial ownership requirements for treaty access. Special economic zone companies and licensed trust administrators must demonstrate genuine business premises, qualified personnel, independent decision-making, and actual management in Egypt; failure to do so can trigger recharacterisation of the arrangement and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Under-Declaration of Fiduciary Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate suppression of management fees or trust administration revenue; recording fictitious service fees or personal expenses as deductible costs; issuing forged Egyptian invoices to reduce taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment in the range of 3 to 5 years and a fine of EGP 100,000 to EGP 500,000 under the Egyptian Income Tax Law and Penal Code; restitution of the evaded tax and monthly late-payment surcharge of 1.5% of unpaid tax up to 100%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, finance officers, and tax representatives face personal criminal liability through veil-piercing where the LLC is used as a facade; the Egyptian Tax Authority may impose travel bans, attachment of personal assets, and confiscation of funds located in Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Asset Protection Trust
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an EG discretionary asset protection trust and a thinly capitalised EG LLC purely as a title-holding and asset-shielding device, with no physical office, employees, bank account in Egypt, independent trustee decision-making, or genuine fiduciary commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian Tax Authority may disregard the trust and LLC as fictitious, reattribute their income to the domestic beneficiary or settlor, impose 22.5% tax on deemed Egyptian-source income, revoke the tax card, and impose fines of up to EGP 2,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may lift the corporate veil; settlors, protectors, and nominee directors are jointly liable for unpaid tax and penalties, and may be made subject to passport surrender, travel bans, and criminal confiscation of Egyptian real estate or bank accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting SWIFT-wired trust assets without proper customer due diligence, failure to identify beneficial owners, non-reporting of suspicious transactions to the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMFCU), or deliberately structuring transactions into amounts below mandatory declaration thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002 and amendments: imprisonment for a period of three months to three years, fines of EGP 50,000 to EGP 200,000, confiscation of the funds, suspension of the required fiduciary or banking license, and closure of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers, directors, trustees, and beneficial owners are personally subject to criminal prosecution; conviction triggers immediate director disqualification, freezing of personal assets, and travel bans pending investigation and appeal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit the TP disclosure schedule attached to the annual corporate tax return, refusal to provide the Local File or Master File during Egyptian Tax Authority scrutiny, or pricing the trust administration fee charged to the non-resident beneficiary at an unrealistic margin unsupported by an approved method.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines not exceeding EGP 1,000,000 or 1% of the controlled transaction amount, plus upward tax adjustment to the arm's length price; the short-paid tax attracts a 1.5% monthly surcharge and the ETA may reopen closed fiscal years where documents are suppressed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax advisers who knowingly direct failure to substantiate transfer pricing may be treated as obstructing tax inspection, leading to personal liability for penalties, disqualification from serving as directors, and judicial enforcement including travel bans and bank attachment.
